title: Sensex Surges Over 2,000 Points Intraday as Record Foreign Inflows Power Rally
excerpt: The Sensex traded up 2.46 per cent by late morning on November 25 and the Nifty hit 25,951.65 intraday, as FIIs extended a 16-session buying streak and November inflows reached a record $13.2 billion.
body:
• The BSE Sensex surged more than 2,000 points in intraday trade on Wednesday, November 25, trading at 84,470.44, up 2,034.45 points or 2.46 per cent, at around 11:45 a.m. IST, according to IANS.
  • The Nifty 50 touched an intraday high of 25,951.65, up 2.37 per cent, as banking, FMCG and IT shares led a broad-based rally.
  • Foreign institutional investors have put a record $13.2 billion into Indian equities so far in November, according to NSDL data cited by market reports, and were net buyers of ₹5,673 crore on Monday.
  • For diaspora investors: the rally follows Monday's sharp fall, and analysts cited by IANS expect continued inflows and earnings momentum to support markets despite global volatility — intraday levels are not closing levels.

Indian equities staged a sharp rebound on Wednesday, November 25, with the BSE Sensex climbing more than 2,000 points in intraday trade as record foreign inflows, falling crude oil prices and buying in banking, technology and FMCG shares lifted the market. At around 11:45 a.m. IST, the Sensex was trading at 84,470.44, up 2,034.45 points or 2.46 per cent, according to IANS. The Nifty 50 touched an intraday high of 25,951.65, up 602 points or 2.37 per cent.

The rally began at the open. The Sensex opened 999.62 points, or 1.21 per cent, higher at 83,435.61, and the Nifty 50 opened up 308.70 points, or 1.22 per cent, at 25,658.35, according to NDTV. By 11:12 a.m., the Sensex was at 84,373.83, up 1,937.84 points or 2.35 per cent from its previous close of 82,435.99, The Hindu BusinessLine reported, with the Nifty at 25,912.10, up 562.45 points. Investor wealth rose by more than ₹4.2 lakh crore in the first hours of trade, according to NDTV. All figures in this report are intraday levels, not closing prices.

"Investor wealth rose by more than ₹4.2 lakh crore in the first hours of trade, according to NDTV."

Foreign money is the engine

Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) have been net buyers in the cash market for 16 consecutive sessions, The Hindu BusinessLine reported, and their November inflows have reached a record $13.2 billion, according to NSDL data. On Monday — a session the market fell sharply — FIIs were still net buyers of ₹5,673 crore, while domestic institutional investors sold ₹2,760 crore, according to exchange data cited by IANS.

Banks, FMCG and IT lead

Financials led the advance: the Nifty Private Bank index rose 2.97 per cent and FMCG gained 2.88 per cent, according to IANS. Technology shares extended their rally for a third consecutive session. The Nifty IT index rose 2.39 per cent, according to NDTV, with Infosys the top gainer among its constituents, up 4.4 per cent, and Tata Consultancy Services up 2.24 per cent, according to Moneycontrol reporting. The Indian rupee strengthened 23 paise to 92.62 against the US dollar, supported by the inflows and softer crude, Moneycontrol reported.

Why India rose while Asia fell

The gains came despite a softer trend across Asia, where a fresh decline in US technology stocks reignited questions about the sustainability of the AI-driven rally; Nvidia fell nearly 6 per cent overnight, according to NDTV. Market participants attributed part of India's strength to rotation out of crowded AI and semiconductor trades into Indian IT services companies, which run asset-light models rather than funding data-centre build-outs. A market expert told NDTV that global investors are rotating into traditional software and IT services companies with stronger cash flows and more attractive valuations.

Domestic earnings provided the other anchor: Nifty 50 companies grew earnings 27 per cent in the second quarter, a figure analysts cited by IANS said could support continued inflows and give the market resilience. The rebound also follows Monday's expiry-driven fall, when the Sensex dropped about 1,484 points — Wednesday's trade, in other words, has recovered that ground and more, at least intraday. What to watch is the close, and whether the foreign buying streak extends to a 17th session.
